changes_made.explanation: Normalized model names by removing redundant variants and simplified output descriptions. All models mentioned are variants of the same core models.
Normalized 'F1 score' to 'F1' as they refer to the same metric. The paper uses F1 score as the primary automatic evaluation metric.
No LLMs were used as judges in this paper (published in 2020, before widespread use of LLM-as-judge paradigm).

guideline: Workers ranked summaries by informativeness and answered six questions about crime investigation aspects (victim revealed, perpetrator identified, cause of death revealed, evidence revealed, motive revealed, crime scene revealed)

changes_made.explanation: Normalized criteria to consistent format with 'revealed/identified' suffix. Removed redundant/overlapping criteria. Added 'crime scene revealed' which was mentioned in the paper but missing from extraction.

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. Main changes involved normalization of model names and evaluation criteria. The paper focuses on extractive summarization of screenplays using narrative structure, with both automatic (F1) and human evaluation. No LLM-based evaluation was used (paper predates that paradigm).
